question: In a patient with early symmetric polyarthritis of the hands, which autoantibody has the HIGHEST specificity for rheumatoid arthritis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ANA is a sensitive but non-specific screening test for systemic autoimmune disease generally — it is positive in SLE, Sjögren's, and many other conditions, including up to 5% of healthy individuals. It is not specific for RA.

RF (IgM anti-IgG antibody) has a sensitivity of ~70% and specificity of ~80% for RA. However, RF is also positive in Sjögren's syndrome, hepatitis C, subacute bacterial endocarditis, and healthy elderly individuals — limiting its specificity.

Correct. Anti-CCP has a specificity of ~95% for RA (higher than RF's ~80%) with comparable sensitivity (~70%). Crucially, anti-CCP can be detected years before clinical arthritis develops and predicts erosive disease — making it the most specific available serological marker for RA.
Anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE, not RA. Its titre also correlates with lupus nephritis activity.

overallFeedback.feedback: Anti-CCP is the most specific serological test for RA (~95% specificity vs RF's ~80%). High-titre positivity of both RF and anti-CCP scores points in the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria and predicts aggressive, erosive disease.

Well done. Anti-CCP (~95% specific) is more specific than RF (~80%) for RA and may be positive years before clinical onset. Together, anti-CCP + RF positivity meets two of the 2010 ACR/EULAR RA classification criteria points.
